title: Independent reading: John 1:1–18
subtitle: Read repeated claims, relative clauses, and theological vocabulary in context.
overview: John’s prologue uses repetition and tightly connected assertions rather than a simple narrative sequence. Map each claim and the links created by relative clauses and conjunctions.
High-density vocabulary deserves slow lexical work: observe its grammatical role in this paragraph before importing broader theological definitions.

items.grc: ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεόν.
items.en: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God.

items.grc: καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν.
items.en: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us.
